name: This Mortal Coil
label: 4AD
lede: Ivo Watts-Russell ran 4AD and wanted to hear his favorite songs played by his own artists, so he made a band with no fixed members and three albums. One Tim Buckley cover outlived all of it.

eras.title: Modern English says no, so Ivo builds a band
eras.text: Ivo Watts-Russell started the label as Axis in November 1979, renamed it 4AD in 1980 and owned it outright by the end of 1981. In 1983 he had an idea for one of his bands, the band passed, and he made the record himself with whoever on the roster would come.

years.h: Watts-Russell and Peter Kent start Axis Records
years.p: It's an imprint of Beggars Banquet, where Watts-Russell had worked since 1977. Early in 1980 it becomes 4AD, short for "forward".
years.xp: Names considered and dropped: 1980AD, 4WD and 1984. Later in 1980 the two bought the label from Beggars Banquet, and by the end of 1981 Kent had sold his stake, leaving Watts-Russell as sole owner. He hired designer [[Vaughan Oliver|2a1b1665-17fc-4ad2-9392-d6fe6788e96e]] and photographer Nigel Grierson, whose 23 Envelope studio would shape how the label looked for two decades.

years.src: Wikipedia: This Mortal Coil · Wikipedia: John Fryer
years.h: Modern English turns down Watts-Russell's medley idea
years.p: He'd asked [[Modern English|78605d0c-7454-456d-934c-51eb46122566]] to re-record Sixteen Days and Gathering Dust as one piece. They declined, so he did it with members of Modern English, [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]] and Cindytalk, and engineer [[John Fryer|17375716-41de-49a9-8b9c-64c71bb14742]].
years.xp: The name comes from a line in Spirit's Dream Within a Dream, itself borrowed from Hamlet. 4AD's own site describes the project as "not a band, but a unique collaboration of musicians recording in various permutations." Watts-Russell and Fryer were the only two constants.

years.h: Sixteen Days / Gathering Dust comes out on 12-inch
years.p: The medley reaches No. 100 in the UK. The B-side gets the attention.

yt: Song to the Siren, official video
years.h: Fraser and Guthrie record Tim Buckley's Song to the Siren
years.p: Watts-Russell promotes it from B-side to single. It reaches No. 66 in the UK, No. 3 on the indie chart, and stays on that chart for 101 weeks.
years.xp: Only [[Elizabeth Fraser|0bf0cabe-def2-4113-8dc5-6e721b9c3a92]]'s voice and [[Robin Guthrie|47d7b25e-585b-4c97-b98b-411b21a53379]]'s guitar are on it. It ranked fourth among all indie singles of the 1980s. The record also sent people back to Tim Buckley's catalogue, and Fraser later recorded a duet with his son, Jeff Buckley.

eras.title: The label boss picks the songs
eras.text: It'll End in Tears and Filigree & Shadow were cut at Blackwing, a converted church in Waterloo, with Fryer engineering and 4AD artists singing Big Star, Roy Harper and Tim Buckley.

years.src: Wikipedia: This Mortal Coil · Wikipedia: It'll End in Tears
years.h: A Big Star song, Kangaroo, becomes the next single
years.p: It's one of two songs from Big Star's Third/Sister Lovers the collective covers, with Holocaust. It reaches No. 2 on the indie chart.

years.cap: Fraser and Guthrie in No.1 magazine, January 1984
years.h: It'll End in Tears reaches No. 1 on the indie chart
years.p: Fraser sings Roy Harper's Another Day, Howard Devoto and [[Lisa Gerrard|cd645207-1664-46af-9953-264e9ae54089]] turn up, and [[Simon Raymonde|54cf21b1-9a02-4a75-a029-3a66db21c545]] plays. It also makes No. 38 on the UK albums chart.
years.xp: Watts-Russell left the arrangements to the musicians. "I loved the experience of affecting the sound of a record, but it wasn't my place to impose anything," he said. Covers include Rema-Rema's Fond Affections and Colin Newman's Not Me; Martin McCarrick plays cello.

years.h: Twenty-five tracks, thirteen without a singer
years.p: Filigree & Shadow is 4AD's first double LP, and it starts the label's DAD catalogue prefix. It peaks at No. 2 on the indie chart.
years.xp: Recorded at Blackwing in London and Palladium in Edinburgh. The covers range from Tim Buckley and Gene Clark to a David Byrne and Brian Eno song, Drugs, which came out with Come Here My Love as a limited single. Vaughan Oliver's v23 designed the sleeve.

eras.title: Blood, and the door closes
eras.text: Five years later the third album drew on 4AD's new American signings too. Then the project stopped.

years.src: Wikipedia: Blood · Wikipedia: This Mortal Coil
years.h: Kim Deal and Tanya Donelly sing Chris Bell on Blood
years.p: [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] of [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]] and [[Tanya Donelly|478e2b34-bda3-48c8-81e4-77efac91f3ec]] of [[Throwing Muses|b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8]] share You and Your Sister. The album reaches No. 28 in the UK, the collective's highest.
years.xp: Caroline Crawley, the Rutkowski sisters Deirdre and Louise, and Alison Limerick sing elsewhere; covers include Syd Barrett and Spirit's Nature's Way. You and Your Sister was released as a single only in the Benelux and France and reached No. 13 in the Netherlands.

years.src: Wikipedia: This Mortal Coil · Wikipedia: John Fryer
years.h: This Mortal Coil ends after three albums
years.p: Fryer has by now produced [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]]' Pretty Hate Machine. Watts-Russell returns to the idea in 1998 as The Hope Blister.

eras.title: A siren in a David Lynch film
eras.text: The records kept circulating after the project stopped, helped by a box set, a film director who'd wanted the song for a decade, and a reissue overseen by the man who started it.

years.cap: A set photo from Lost Highway, 1997
yt: The Song to the Siren scene in Lost Highway
years.h: Song to the Siren plays in Lost Highway
years.p: David Lynch had wanted the song for Blue Velvet in 1986 but couldn't afford the licence, and wrote Mysteries of Love with Angelo Badalamenti instead. It's in the film but not on the soundtrack album.

years.h: Watts-Russell sells 4AD and moves to New Mexico
years.p: He sells his stake to Martin Mills of the Beggars Group and settles in Santa Fe. He prefers the title "musical director" to producer.

years.src: Wikipedia: This Mortal Coil · Wikipedia: Filigree
years.h: The catalogue is reissued as four HDCDs
years.p: The box, This Mortal Coil, is followed on August 6, 2012 by Dust & Guitars, a set of rarities.
